data.name: Jitesh
data.gender_notes: Jitesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jitesh is derived from the Sanskrit words 'jit' meaning victory and 'ish' meaning lord or bringer. The name is bestowed upon a child born to parents who have recently experienced a significant victory or triumph, or to one who is expected to bring success and prosperity to the family. The name Jitesh carries the meaning “Victory Bringer” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jitesh usually hope their child will grow to embody victory bringer and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jitesh total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jitesh holds significant cultural importance in Hindu traditions as it reflects the courage, strength, and determination of the parents or the child themselves. It is believed that a child named Jitesh will embody these qualities, bringing victory and triumph to their family and community. The use of this name also highlights the importance of celebrating achievements and victories in Indian culture.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Jitesh is believed to bring blessings of victory, courage, and strength from the gods. It is thought to symbolize the power of the divine within the individual, reinforcing the idea that we all have the potential to overcome obstacles and achieve great things with the help of the divine. By giving their child the name Jitesh, parents are acknowledging the role of the divine in their victory and seeking its continued guidance and support in their lives.

vedic_reference.note: The name Jitesh is derived from the Sanskrit words 'jita' (victory) and 'ish' (bringer). It is the name of the Sun God, Surya, who is believed to bring victory and success in life.

historical_references.reference: Jitesh was a prominent Jain monk and scholar in medieval India, active in the 12th and 13th centuries. He wrote several commentaries on the Jain Agamas and is known for his contributions to Jain philosophy and literature.

Jitesh was also the name of a powerful Rajput king in the late 15th and early 16th centuries, ruling over the kingdom of Marwar (Jodhpur). He expanded his territory through military conquests and is remembered for his patronage of arts and architecture.
